schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The JOIN between three things that already existed separately and never met: a ticket's falsifier clauses, a proof's declaration of which clauses it covers, and the tester's seal saying which of that proof's teeth actually ran green. `clauses(ticket)` splits a falsifier's `proves_red` into its numbered clauses (a flat falsifier is one clause named `all`; everything after WRONG INTENT is dropped, because a disposition is not a condition a tooth goes green on). `declared(proof_path)` reads a module-level `PROVES = {ticket_id: {clause: tooth}}` block by AST — never by import, so reading a declaration cannot run the proof. `teeth_printed(stdout)` extracts the tooth names a proof marked green and red from its FULL stdout. `lacks(ticket, repo_root=...)` returns the named gaps: no proof, no proof on disk, a proof declaring nothing for this ticket, an undeclared clause named by its number, a declared tooth the seal never recorded green, no seal, a seal whose source fingerprint has gone stale. A concept-piece takes the other branch — its coverage question is whether a REVIEW validation sits beside the artifact, not a clause join. It holds no state and consults nothing but files it is handed.
why: MEASURED 2026-09-07: four of twelve tickets at PROVEME named a proof that never mentions their subject — three of them named `test_trouble_panel.py`, a green-sealed proof containing no tooth about any of the three. THE LIVED SYMPTOM: a builder crosses a ticket to PROVEME, names the proof that happens to sit beside the code he touched, and the crossing is accepted because the proof is green. Nothing anywhere asked whether that green says anything about THIS ticket. So proven-space fills with tickets whose evidence is real, sealed, current — and about something else. That is a hollow green (Law 8), and a hollow green is worse than a red, because a peer leans on it: the whole return on proving first is composing proven code WITHOUT re-checking it, and this defect spends that return on nothing. The corpus-wide shape is the same failure at scale — 215 of 230 tickets in proven-space name no proof at all.
invoke: `from cairn.tools import proof_coverage` — composed by the sieve (`proof_covers_the_ticket` in machines/build_inspector) and by the tester (`teeth_printed`, to fill `evidence.teeth_green` on every seal). No CLI door: it answers a question about artifacts, it is not run at a person. Prove: `python3 cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proofs/test_proof_coverage.py`.
entry: FRESH build, 2026-09-07, ticket feeb4c786b14. Nothing grafted. The seal read composes `cairn/tools/base/validation.latest_seal` (the established read-side door to the tester's validation store) rather than re-deriving a path into `devices/tester`. The AST-not-import discipline is the same one `intentions_model_compiler` uses on charters, cited not copied.
state_and_history: state.json + history.json beside this charter, born at the ticket's BUILDME crossing on 2026-09-07 through harbor_master.clearance.clear.
how_it_learns: IT DOESN'T, BECAUSE THE JOIN IS A JOIN: a coverage check that adjusted its own strictness would be exactly the negotiation a deterministic red exists to refuse. What learns is the CORPUS it reads — the count of uncovered tickets is a measurement that moves as tickets are remediated, and its trend is the reading. The one place a parameter could drift is the marker vocabulary (`GREEN_MARKERS`/`RED_MARKERS`), and that is deliberately NOT learned: it keys on a marker word beside a `test_`-shaped name rather than on a roster of the five printing styles measured in the corpus, because a hand roster beside the corpus it lists goes stale in the green-looking direction.
filed_edges: (a) A PROOF WITHOUT `PROVES` IS RED, NOT EXEMPT (Law 9). Measured 2026-09-07: 189 proof files in the corpus, and the number carrying a PROVES block at the moment this shipped was zero. Every declaration is therefore a debt being paid down, and the sieve's count is the ledger. A tool that let an undeclared proof pass would have shipped green on day one and measured nothing.

(b) THE DECLARATION IS UNCHECKED AGAINST THE TOOTH'S CONTENT. `PROVES` says tooth X covers clause (2); nothing verifies that tooth X's assertions have anything to do with clause (2). This is the residual hollow: a builder can declare a lie. What the join DOES remove is the accidental version — the green that was never about this ticket and nobody noticed — which is the failure actually measured. Closing the rest needs a reader, which means cognition, which is a different ticket.

(c) CLAUSE NUMBERS ARE READ FROM `(N)` MARKERS IN PROSE. A falsifier that numbers its conditions some other way (`1.`, `first`, bullets) reads as one clause named `all`. That is a true reading — an unnumbered falsifier genuinely offers nothing finer to join on — but it is quieter than it should be: the ticket looks covered by one tooth when it may need four.

(d) `crossing_record_absent` IS ARCHAEOLOGY, NOT A DEFECT ANYONE INTRODUCED. 196 PROVED tickets carry no crossings array at all, because they reached proven-space before the crossing record existed. They are red — Law 9 has no `pre-existing` triage authority — but they are split into their own lack kind so nineteen actionable tickets are not buried under two hundred archaeological ones.

(e) THE SIEVE READS THE COMMONS FROM CLASS-SPACE. `proof_covers_the_ticket` derives `CairnCommons` as a sibling of the repo root. A checkout without the commons beside it reports zero findings, which reads as green — the one place this instrument can go quiet for the wrong reason.
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_proof_coverage.py: 20 teeth. The five the ticket's falsifier names, each declared in this proof's own PROVES block; plus the green halves that keep every red half falsifiable (a fully covered fixture produces NO finding; a concept-piece WITH a review record is covered); plus two wrong-intent teeth (a marker word in prose mints no tooth; reading a declaration does not execute the proof, checked with a proof that writes a file if run). Durability gate: committed + pushed.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a sealed proof's `evidence.teeth_green` omits a tooth the proof printed green — in particular a 40-tooth proof sealing only the 20 the `stdout_tail` holds; (2) a ticket at PROVEME whose named proof declares clause (1) of a two-clause falsifier does not red naming clause (2) specifically; (3) a fixture whose proof declares every clause, whose declared teeth are all green in the seal, and whose fingerprint matches, produces any finding; (4) any ticket in proven-space is neither covered nor named with an actionable lack — silent absence is the failure this replaced; (5) a concept-piece at PROVEME with no review VALIDATION beside its artifact does not red `no review record`, or one WITH a review record reds. WRONG-INTENT SIGNAL: a `PROVES` block for one ticket routinely exceeding ~8 lines, which would mean the declaration has become a second copy of the falsifier rather than a pointer into it; or a marker word appearing in ordinary prose minting a tooth that does not exist, which would turn coverage green on names nobody wrote.
proof: proofs/test_proof_coverage.py — clause (1) runs the REAL tester through the REAL door on a 40-tooth fixture rather than parsing a canned string, because the claim is about what `run_proof` records and a canned string would prove only that the parser works on strings I wrote. Clause (4) runs over the LIVE corpus and asserts the INVARIANT (no ticket in proven-space escapes unnamed; every finding carries an actionable lack) rather than the snapshot count 19, which moves as tickets cross. The proof declares its own coverage of the ticket that built it — the one tooth that fails if the AST reader stops finding PROVES blocks, which every other tooth would survive.

feedback.why: An uncovered ticket in proven-space is a care-of-the-code finding: it is the corpus claiming a green it cannot support. codemother owns the care of the code and reviews adversarially toward it; the sieve's findings ride the build_inspector's `uncovered_tickets` key into the operator inbox, naming the ticket and the specific lack.

owner: A TOOL HAS USERS, NOT AN OWNER (Law 6). Akien owns the definition — that a proof must say what it proves, and that a ticket naming a proof which says nothing about it is red. CC writes the code and the proofs.
traces_to: Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass — this is the check that the proof was about the thing)
Law 3 (nothing is known until measured — a seal whose fingerprint has gone stale is a closed horizon, not standing evidence)
Law 9 (red is the default; an undeclared proof is red, and there is no pre-existing triage authority for the 196 that predate the record)
Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics — the join is a sieve, not a reminder in a review checklist)
Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel — nobody should have to re-read a proof to learn whether it covers the ticket that named it)
provenance: Born 2026-09-07 from ticket feeb4c786b14, cast through the /sorted door. The measurement that bore it: four of twelve PROVEME tickets named proofs that never mention their subject, three of them the same proof.
learns: It does not; it is a pure join over files it is handed. The corpus it reads is what moves.
